content: Python ints have arbitrary precision and never overflow like C ints.
Compare against None with `is`, never `==`.
Mutable default arguments are created once and shared across calls; use None instead.
In Python, empty collections, zero, None and False are all falsy.
Loop-else runs only when the loop exits without break.
Prefer enumerate() and zip() over manual index bookkeeping in for loops.
Python argument passing is call-by-object-reference: mutation is visible, rebinding is not.
Names assigned inside a function are local unless declared global/nonlocal (LEGB).
Parameters after a bare * in the signature are keyword-only.
Comprehension loop variables have their own scope and do not leak.
Generator expressions are lazy and use constant memory for one-pass pipelines.
any()/all() short-circuit, pairing well with generator expressions.
Dict and set lookup/insert/delete are O(1) on average via hashing.
Dict keys must be hashable; mutating a key would strand its entry.
list(dict.fromkeys(items)) deduplicates while preserving order.
Python str methods return new strings; strings are immutable.
Use ''.join(pieces) instead of += in a loop to avoid O(n^2) concatenation.
UTF-8 encode/decode at system boundaries; never mix str and bytes.
Names assigned in the class body are shared class attributes, not per-instance state.
@property exposes a method as attribute-style access.
Python has no true private attributes; _x is convention, __x is name-mangled.
Python resolves methods via C3 linearization; check ClassName.__mro__.
Defining __eq__ without __hash__ makes instances unhashable.
Always implement __repr__; it is what appears in tracebacks and logs.
Any function containing yield returns a generator object when called.
Generators are single-pass; a consumed generator yields nothing more.
for loops and unpacking both run on the iterator protocol (__iter__/__next__).
@dec is exactly f = dec(f), executed at function definition time.
functools.wraps preserves the wrapped function's name and docstring.
Stacked decorators apply bottom-up; the top one is outermost.
The with statement guarantees __exit__ runs even when exceptions occur.
@contextlib.contextmanager builds a manager from a generator with yield.
Never rely on __del__ for cleanup; its timing is not guaranteed.
Bare except swallows KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit; always catch specific types.
raise X from err chains exceptions so the original cause stays visible.
assert is for internal invariants; it is stripped by python -O.
import executes a module once and caches it in sys.modules.
if __name__ == '__main__' lets a file work both imported and as a script.
Never name your script after a stdlib module; it shadows the real one.
python -m venv .venv creates an isolated environment per project.
Pin dependencies with == and pip freeze for reproducible installs.
Never sudo pip install into system Python; it conflicts with the OS package manager.
Type hints are ignored at runtime; checkers like mypy verify them statically.
int | None is the modern spelling of Optional[int] (Python 3.10+).
Protocol enables structural typing: duck typing the checker can verify.
Dataclass mutable defaults require field(default_factory=...).
@dataclass(frozen=True) creates immutable, hashable value objects.
__post_init__ runs after the generated __init__ for validation.
collections.deque gives O(1) append/pop on both ends; list.pop(0) is O(n).
Counter(words).most_common(n) ranks frequencies in one expression.
deque(maxlen=n) auto-discards oldest items: a sliding window.
itertools.groupby clusters only consecutive equal keys; sort first for global groups.
Infinite iterators (count/cycle/repeat) must always be bounded with islice.
functools.lru_cache memoizes pure functions; args must be hashable.
pathlib joins paths with the / operator, portably across OSes.
Always pass encoding explicitly to Path.read_text()/write_text().
Joining with an absolute right side discards the left: Path('/a')/'/b' -> /b.
os.replace() renames atomically: readers never see a half-written file.
os.environ.get('KEY', default) avoids KeyError on missing config.
Prefer subprocess.run([...]) over os.system to avoid shell injection.
Pass commands as a list to subprocess.run to avoid shell injection.
check=True makes subprocess.run raise on nonzero exit instead of failing silently.
Always set timeout= on subprocess calls; always reap Popen children with communicate()/wait().
argparse converts, validates (type/choices), and generates --help automatically.
Subparsers give git-style subcommands, each with its own arguments.
Keep parsing thin and logic in plain functions so CLIs stay testable.
Only basic types round-trip through JSON natively; convert datetimes etc. explicitly.
Open CSV files with newline='' and let the csv module handle line endings.
csv.DictReader keys rows by header names, immune to column reordering.
Write regex patterns as raw strings: r'\\d+' not '\\d+'.
re.fullmatch requires the entire string to match; re.match anchors only the start.
Never parse nested formats like HTML with regex; use a real parser.
Store and compute in UTC; convert to local time only for display.
Comparing naive and aware datetimes raises TypeError.
time.monotonic() measures durations; time.time() gives wall-clock timestamps.
Use lazy %-style args in log calls so messages build only when emitted.
Libraries should get loggers but never configure logging.
log.exception inside except blocks logs the message plus traceback.
Arrange-act-assert is the standard test structure: setup, execute, verify.
Mock external boundaries (network, filesystem, clocks) so tests stay fast and deterministic.
pytest.mark.parametrize runs one test body over many inputs.
CPython's GIL means threads do not parallelize CPU-bound Python code.
Threads excel at I/O-bound work; the GIL is released during I/O waits.
Use Queue for thread-safe handoff instead of shared state plus manual locks.
multiprocessing bypasses the GIL with separate processes for CPU-bound work.
Worker functions must be importable top-level functions (picklable by reference).
Guard pool creation with if __name__ == '__main__' to prevent spawn loops.
socket.send() may transmit partial data; use sendall() for full delivery.
TCP recv() returns whatever arrived; loop until the message is complete or b'' arrives.
Always set timeouts on network calls; the default waits forever.
Never interpolate values into SQL strings; use ? placeholders to prevent injection.
The with conn: block commits on clean exit and rolls back on exception.
SQLite needs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON per connection to enforce foreign keys.
Never store passwords as plain SHA-256; use pbkdf2_hmac, bcrypt, or argon2 with unique salts.
Use the secrets module, never random, for tokens and passwords.
Compare HMAC digests with hmac.compare_digest to avoid timing leaks.
In bash, single quotes prevent all expansion; double quotes allow $var and $(cmd).
set -euo pipefail makes scripts fail fast on errors, unset vars, and pipeline failures.
Exit status 0 means success; test with if cmd directly, not just $?.
cmd >file 2>&1 merges stderr into the file; the order of redirections matters.
Pipeline stages run in subshells; variables set there do not survive.
find -print0 | xargs -0 safely handles filenames with spaces/newlines.
grep -F treats the pattern as a fixed string: faster, no metacharacter surprises.
awk processes whitespace/comma-delimited fields: $1, $2, NR, NF.
Single-quote shell patterns so the shell does not expand them first.
find ... -print0 | xargs -0 cmd is the whitespace-safe bulk pattern.
Preview with -print before any destructive find action like -delete.
xargs -P N runs N parallel workers for bulk jobs.
Permission triples are user/group/other, each rwx; 755 executables, 644 files, 600 secrets.
Never chmod 777; diagnose the actual missing bit instead.
Every parent directory needs the x bit for path traversal; use namei -l to debug.
SIGTERM (15) asks a process to exit cleanly; SIGKILL (9) forces it with no cleanup.
Always try SIGTERM before SIGKILL.
Zombie processes are dead children unreaped by their parent; fix the parent.
Use ed25519 keys with passphrases; disable password auth once keys work.
Private SSH keys must be 600 and never shared or committed.
Never blindly accept a changed host key; verify out-of-band first.
In rsync, src/ copies contents; src copies the directory itself.
Always dry-run (rsync -n) before --delete; it mirrors destructively.
List tarballs (tar -t) and extract into a fresh dir to dodge tarbombs.
Cron runs with a minimal environment; use absolute paths and set PATH in the crontab.
systemctl status + journalctl -u name is the service debugging order.
systemd timers support jitter and Persistent catch-up runs; cron does not.
export shares a variable with child processes; without it the variable is shell-local.
~/.bashrc runs for interactive shells; ~/.profile for login shells.
Never put '.' in PATH; it enables trojan-horse executables.
A 'full' disk with free bytes usually means exhausted inodes; check df -i.
In free -h, 'available' is the meaningful number; cache is not a leak.
Deleted-but-open files still occupy space until the holder closes them.
Debug connectivity bottom-up: DNS, then ping, then port, then HTTP.
ss -tlnp lists listening TCP ports and owning processes.
Never pipe curl output directly to a shell without inspecting it first.
git init creates a repo; git clone copies one with full history and an origin remote.
Set user.name/user.email before committing; commits without identity are misattributed.
A committed secret is compromised once pushed; rotate it, do not just delete the file.
git add -p stages interactively hunk-by-hunk for one-idea-per-commit.
git diff --cached shows exactly what the next commit will contain.
Never amend or rewrite history that others have based work on.
A git branch is a lightweight pointer to a commit; creating one is nearly free.
git branch -d refuses to delete unmerged branches as a safety net.
Keep branches short-lived; long branches accumulate painful merge drift.
Golden rule: never rebase commits that others have based work on.
git pull --rebase replays local commits onto the fetched tip without noise merges.
Use --force-with-lease instead of --force; it refuses when others pushed.
git stash push -m 'msg' shelves work; pop restores onto the current branch.
Stash -u includes untracked files; default stashes tracked changes only.
Stash is for short parking; longer work belongs on a real branch.
git fetch downloads remote history without touching your work; pull = fetch + integrate.
--force-with-lease only rewrites if the remote matches what you last saw.
Inspect with git log origin/main..main before integrating remote changes.
git log -S 'text' finds commits that added or removed a string (pickaxe).
git diff --cached shows staged changes; plain diff shows unstaged.
A...B (three dots) shows changes unique to either side since the merge base.
git revert creates a new commit undoing an old one: safe for shared history.
git reset --hard permanently discards uncommitted work; verify status first.
git reflog records HEAD movements for ~90 days: the rescue tool for lost commits.
Prefer annotated tags (-a) over lightweight; sign release tags (-s).
git push --follow-tags pushes commits plus their tags.
Never move a published tag; cut a new version instead.
Protect main: require reviews, green CI, no direct pushes.
Keep pull requests small and focused for fast, real reviews.
Main stays releasable at all times; broken main blocks everyone.
Big-O describes growth rate, dropping constants and lower-order terms.
Nested loops over the same n give O(n^2); a hash map often reduces it to O(n).
State best/average/worst case; quicksort is O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst.
Python's sorted()/list.sort() use Timsort: stable, adaptive, O(n log n).
Stable sorts preserve the order of equal elements, enabling multi-key sorts.
Many problems reduce to sort + one linear pass (e.g., two-sum with two pointers).
Binary search needs sorted data and runs in O(log n) time.
Exclude mid each step (lo=mid+1/hi=mid-1) or the loop may never terminate.
Use the bisect module for insertion points instead of hand-rolling.
Every recursion needs a base case and a step that shrinks toward it.
Python has no tail-call optimization and a ~1000-frame recursion limit.
Memoization (lru_cache) turns exponential naive recursion into polynomial time.
Use list as a stack (append/pop) and deque as a queue (popleft).
list.pop(0) is O(n); deque.popleft() is O(1).
heapq provides a min-heap priority queue with O(log n) push/pop.
Linked lists give O(1) insert/delete at a known node but O(i) access to index i.
Python lists are dynamic arrays and beat linked lists for nearly all real uses.
Fast/slow pointers detect cycles and find midpoints in one pass.
BST inorder traversal yields values in sorted order.
A degenerate (unbalanced) BST degrades to O(n) per operation.
heapq.nlargest(k, nums) finds top-k in O(n log k) without full sort.
BFS on unweighted graphs finds shortest paths; first visit is via the shortest route.
DFS and BFS are both O(V + E); a visited set is mandatory on cyclic graphs.
Grids are graphs: treat cells as vertices and moves as edges.
Hash tables give O(1) average insert/lookup/delete via key hashing.
Equal objects must hash equal; keys must stay immutable while stored.
Python randomizes string hashing to defend against hash-flooding attacks.
DP needs optimal substructure plus overlapping subproblems.
Define the state precisely (dp[i] = exact meaning) before writing the recurrence.
lru_cache turns naive exponential recursion into polynomial DP.
Threads share the process's address space; processes have separate ones.
The kernel schedules threads; N threads can run on N cores simultaneously.
fork duplicates a process (copy-on-write); exec replaces its image.
Stack frames are automatic and fast but small; heap objects have flexible lifetimes.
Returning a pointer to a stack local (C) creates a dangling pointer.
In Python every object is heap-allocated and freed by refcount + cycle collector.
The MMU translates per-process virtual addresses to physical RAM via page tables.
Copy-on-write makes fork cheap by sharing pages until one side writes.
Thrashing (working set > RAM) collapses throughput; the fix is less memory pressure.
Filenames live in directories; inodes hold metadata and block pointers.
Hard links share one inode; symlinks are path strings that can break.
Check df -i for inode exhaustion when a disk reports full with free bytes.
SIGTERM (15) requests graceful shutdown; SIGKILL (9) forces it and cannot be caught.
Signal handlers must be tiny and reentrant: set a flag, return.
SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored.
Fds 0/1/2 are stdin/stdout/stderr; the same read/write works on files, sockets, pipes.
Leaked descriptors cause 'too many open files'; check /proc/<pid>/fd.
dup2 remaps descriptors: the mechanism behind shell redirection.
TCP provides reliability via handshake, sequence numbers, ACKs, and retransmission.
TCP is a byte stream; it does not preserve application message boundaries.
Private IPv4 ranges: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 (not globally routable).
TCP: reliable ordered byte stream. UDP: connectionless best-effort datagrams.
UDP suits timeliness-over-completeness (media, DNS, games); TCP suits must-arrive-in-order data.
QUIC runs reliable streams over UDP, eliminating TCP head-of-line blocking.
DNS resolves via root -> TLD -> authoritative hierarchy, with TTL-based caching.
Lower DNS TTLs before migrations; caches hold old values until expiry.
Test DNS first when debugging connectivity: dig +short, and dig @8.8.8.8 to bypass local resolvers.
HTTP status classes: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
GET/HEAD must be safe (no state change); PUT/DELETE should be idempotent.
HTTP is stateless; sessions ride on cookies or tokens.
Never disable TLS certificate verification to work around an error.
TLS clients must verify chain, hostname (SAN), dates, and revocation.
Forward secrecy (ECDHE) keeps past traffic safe even if long-term keys leak.
Ports below 1024 are privileged: binding them requires root.
Connection refused = nothing listening; timeout = filtered or black-holed.
Firewall posture: default-deny inbound, allow only needed ports from needed sources.
